- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model shows persistent bias toward mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misjudges momentum; align forecast with sentiment swing direction, not absolute trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to match recent average unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
